title: Naval Communications and Systems Master Recall Flashcards
description: Comprehensive active-recall flashcard deck designed to test your mastery of Safety, Hardware Nomenclatures, Satellites, Signal Propagation, Data Links, CDLMS, Aegis BMD, and administrative timelines.

flashcards.back: Electric current passing through the body (Amperage), NOT voltage. Voltage is simply the pressure that pushes the current through a path of least resistance.
Severity is directly proportional to (Current * Time) / Body Resistance. Prolonged exposure and low resistance (e.g., wet/damaged skin) drastically increase injury severity.
Hand-to-hand or hand-to-foot. These paths channel current straight through the chest and heart, causing Ventricular Fibrillation (a disorganized rhythm preventing blood flow).

flashcards.front: First Responder Flow for Electrical Shock
flashcards.back: (1) Isolate/turn off power or switch to STANDBY; (2) Insulate yourself; (3) Disconnect victim using non-conductive tools (wooden board, boot); (4) Never touch victim's skin directly; (5) Contact 911/Medical.
Stop all work aloft immediately if the ship rolls >= 10 degrees or if winds exceed 30 knots (noted as 30 nautical miles in collaborative class notes).

flashcards.front: Height Limit for Safety Observers aloft
flashcards.back: A safety observer is mandatory when personnel are working aloft or anywhere higher than 5 feet off the deck.
Must be passed prior to personnel ascending and repeated every 15 minutes: 'Do not rotate antennas, energize or radiate any electrical or electronic equipment while personnel are working aloft.'
Console transmitters/radars must be in STANDBY. Hang physical signs reading 'Secured Personnel Aloft' indicating date, time, and climber's initials.

flashcards.front: Yellow Caution Tag vs. Red Danger Tag
flashcards.back: Yellow Caution Tag (6 fields) provides temporary, special operating instructions. Red Danger Tag (5 fields) completely prohibits the operation of the component to safeguard sailors and gear.
Out of Commission (OOC) sticker has 5 fields. Out of Calibration (CAL) sticker has 6 fields, including the offset 'Correction' value.
[Department]-[Division]-[Sequential Number] (e.g., ENG-DANGER-0001). Tags can never be reused, nor used for simple component ID or leak marking.
CSOOW and EOOW/EDO must verbally coordinate tagouts affecting: (1) interior/monitoring communications, (2) electronic cooling loops, (3) service/high-pressure air, (4) fire main.
Rubber insulated boots protect up to 600V (no exposed metal). Rubber insulating gloves are rated by wall thickness and voltage, split into Classes 0, 1, 2, and 3.
Hearing PPE is mandatory at noise levels >= 85 dB. Continuous exposure limit is 140 dB over 8 hours. Personal music players/earbuds are banned in noise-hazard zones.
Air-purifying respirators are mandatory when working with paints/solvents, but only safe if oxygen is >= 22% by volume (unventilated spaces require extreme caution).
A bright red cabinet voice switch. Connects cryptographic interface units to TA-978 red phones in secure voice circuits only.
Switches digital and analog interfaces and can establish tactical voice conference calls.
RED indicates decrypted/unencrypted (Plain Text) paths. BLACK indicates encrypted (Cipher Text) paths. Interconnects RF components physically.
A commercial satellite RF modem manufactured by Comtech EF Data, used shipboard for digital RF transmissions.
TD-1271 combines 4 signals at 16 kbps each in UHF DAMA circuits. TD-1063 demultiplexes/separates composite signals for the Fleet Satellite Broadcast.
A handheld fill device used to load Cryptographic Keying Material (KEYMAT) into switches and crypto units.
Low Earth Orbit (400 to 1,600 miles altitude). Requires significantly less energy to transmit and receive signals due to proximity.
Medium Earth Orbit. Synchronous orbit situated between 1,500 and 6,500 miles above Earth.
Highly Elliptical Orbit. Asynchronous, highly elliptical 24,000-mile orbit with a fast, close approach at 900 miles.
Located exactly 22,500 miles up. Travels at the exact speed of Earth's rotation to remain stationary over one meridian.
300 MHz to 3 GHz. Mapped as HLL: High mobility, Low capacity (64 Kbps), Low anti-jam. Vulnerable to jamming and nuclear radiation.
3 GHz to 30 GHz. Mapped as HLM: Low mobility, High capacity (up to 155 Mbps), Moderate anti-jam.
30 GHz to 300 GHz. Mapped as HMH: Moderate mobility, High capacity, High anti-jam. Nuclear survivable but heavily degraded by rain/weather.
LDR (Low Data Rate: 75 bps to 2.4 Kbps), MDR (Medium Data Rate: up to 1.544 Mbps), and XDR (Extended Data Rate: up to 8.192 Mbps).
Inversely proportional. Frequency (Hz) Up = Wavelength (feet) Down. Higher frequency waves carry more energy, but propagation range is path-dependent.
Surface to 6-10 miles. Lowest layer containing all weather systems. Directly attenuates (scatters/absorbs) space wave and RF propagation.
10 to 30 miles altitude. Sits between Troposphere and Ionosphere. Highly stable, constant temperature, little to no effect on RF propagation.
Daylight solar UV splits the F layer (90-250 miles) into F1 and F2 sublayers. At night, they merge back into one F layer. This region is the primary driver for long-distance skywave HF.
Directly limits surface wave range. Rocky terrain exhibits low conductivity (high attenuation). Seawater exhibits maximum conductivity (minimal signal loss).
Voice RX Path: RF -> IF -> AF (audio frequency: 20Hz-20kHz). Data RX Path: RF -> IF -> DC (direct current representing binary states).
DTE (router/terminal) generates/consumes user data. DCE (modem) interfaces with the network and ALWAYS provides the clock rate on classic synchronous links.
TADIL-A. Range is ~150 nautical miles ship-to-air. Uses HF (BLOS) or UHF (LOS). Coordinated via the non-secure voice circuit LINK COORD.
TADIL-J. Secure, high-capacity, jam-resistant tactical backbone using J-series message packets and a pseudo-random frequency-hopping pattern.
Point-to-point, two-way, near-real-time data and voice LOS connection between ships (CG, DDG) and SH-60 helicopters (VHF LOS).
Both fall under JREAP-C (SHF). MTJ (Multicast J) is secure, low-latency, group (one-to-many) distribution via satellite. UTJ (Unicast J) is secure, direct point-to-point (one-to-one).

flashcards.front: CDLMS Upper Chassis (C4S A) vs. Lower Chassis (SYS B)
flashcards.back: Upper Chassis (C4S A) handles message processing, time-tagging, database normalization, routing, and Link 11-16 forwarding. Lower Chassis (SYS B) houses data-terminal hardware and converts digital-analog signals.
Consolidates hardware footprints. Remote session is routed directly to the CND display, retiring the physical HMI console, and replacing the MDU with the NIMACS console.
DETECT (phased-array AN/SPY-1 tracking >100 targets simultaneously) -> TRACK -> DESTROY/INTERCEPT (SM-3 midcourse/exo-atmospheric intercept vs. SM-2 terminal/endgame phase defense).

flashcards.front: Aegis BMD Watchstander Rates (IT, ET, FCA, GM)
flashcards.back: IT (operates comms/networks), ET (maintains antennas/C2ISR), FCA (operates SPY-1 radar/Aegis computers), GM (operates VLS/missiles).

flashcards.front: Aegis BMD CIC Stations (TAO, BMDO, RSC, MSS, ADWC)
flashcards.back: TAO (overall tactical weapon leader), BMDO (reporting/liaison to POTUS), RSC (controls SPY-1 radar), MSS (fires interceptors/VLS supervisor), ADWC (air defense coordination).
A cross-rate troubleshooting team (IT, ET, FC, OS, GM) that immediately responds to investigate and restore down data links.
Must be submitted to RSSC/GSSC 30 to 60 days prior to underway (with a strict 21-day absolute minimum).
OPTASK COMMS is generated 7-10 days prior by the OTC (battle group wide). COMMPLAN is ship-specific and completed 72 hours prior by the COMMO.
Daily COMMSTAT (2301) is broadcast by NCTAMS at 2301 ZULU daily. COMSPOT is an outage report sent after 30 minutes of communication disruption, updated hourly on the hour.
Must be completed and submitted to NCTAMS within 10 days of mission completion to prevent delay/denial of future satellite access requests.
